daily_thesis: The August 3 backfill says that robot policies are no longer failing only because they lack scale; they fail because temporal critic state, camera geometry, action-relevant futures, and sparse moving-object geometry are untyped. WCM, RayViT, ST-WAM, and CorrelationFlow point to the same operating model: before APRL collects more demonstrations, it should expose the hidden state channel that the next action actually depends on.

clusters.cluster: VLA repair moves from action heads to critic and safety state
clusters.why: WCM makes the critic history-aware, FibVLA changes temporal sampling, ST-WAM asks whether future state survives visual shift, ActFovea safeguards visual-action consistency at runtime, and barrier-enhanced flow matching adds an explicit safety layer. The shared decision is to type the state that makes a VLA update trustworthy.
clusters.confidence_note: Multiple VLA papers independently expose critic, temporal, WAM, and safety-state variables.
clusters.lab_action: Run one VLA with critic-history, temporal sampling, visual-shift WAM, and runtime safety gates toggled separately under the same manipulation tasks.
